values: Fictional materials: a first-year senior secondary mathematics lesson on linear equations

M1｜A completely fictional class of 20 students, B01. The teaching objective is solving linear equations with brackets; it contains no real student identities or grades. This exercise uses original equations and is simulated on paper only.

M2｜Pre-lesson question 2(x−3)=10, with reference solution x=8. Of the 20 students, 7 answered correctly (35%) and 13 did not; without the individual answers of those 13, the specific error cause cannot be determined.

M3｜Exit question 3(x−2)=12, with reference solution x=6. 13/20 answered correctly (65%); another 4 fictional answers expand the brackets as 3x+6=12→x=2, and 3 answers read 3x−6=12→3x=12−6→x=2. The two categories are mutually exclusive and total 20 students.
M4｜Pre-lesson goal: after the lesson, at least 80% correct on a similar exit question and the ability to point out the two common error types; the goal must be written before seeing the results.

M5｜Next question 4(x−1)=20, with reference solution x=6. 16/20 answered correctly (80%) and 4 did not; the numerical threshold in M4 is met, but without paired data this does not prove individual progress or a teaching cause.

M6｜Question difficulty, marking criteria and student attendance may change; the same basis, anonymous answers and question answers must be verified. Formal assessment is handed to the subject teacher per school procedures.
Task: calculate, explain and review

T1｜Calculate the correct rates for M2, M3 and M5 and the percentage-point change of M3 relative to M2; judge whether 
M3 and M5 meet the pre-set 80%.

T2｜Against the two given answers in M3, point out the bracket sign expansion error and the transposition equation error respectively, write feedback and one original re-check question (with your own answer); explain the basis limits in M6.
Reference answer and boundaries

M2 7/20=35%; M3 13/20=65%; M5 16/20=80%. M3 is 30 percentage points higher than M2; M3 did not reach 
80% while M5 did.

M3 the two error types have given processes: 3(x−2) should expand to 3x−6; 3x−6=12 requires adding 6 to both sides to give 3x=18. A re-check question can be 2(x−4)=6 with answer x=7; first verify the negative sign and the operation on both sides, then look at the student's new answer, and do not infer fixed ability from headcounts.

The three class proportions have no paired student data or control group, so they cannot be used to assert that every student improved or that the lesson caused the improvement; first verify the questions and attendance.
Review checklist

Pre-lesson: 7 correct +13 incorrect = 20; post-lesson: 13 correct +4 bracket sign errors +3 transposition errors = 20; M5 is 16 correct +4 incorrect = 20. The pre-lesson 7 and post-lesson 13 belong to different times and cannot be added to prove a total or individual progress. Distinguish correct rate, percentage points, the pre-set goal and causation.
